# Quality Gate Checklist: Feature 002 — Multi-Format Audio Library

**Purpose**: Reviewer-owned requirements-quality gate and acceptance validation before implementation and PR merge  
**Created**: 2026-09-20  
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md) | **Plan**: [plan.md](../plan.md)  

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.  
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.  
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does NOT mean implementation work is complete.  

---

## 1. Requirement Completeness

- [ ] CHK001 - Are all baseline audio formats (MP3, FLAC, WAV, AAC, M4A, OGG, Opus, WMA, AIFF, APE, WavPack, DSD .dsf/.dff, Musepack) explicitly enumerated in the requirements? [Completeness, Spec §FR-002]
- [ ] CHK002 - Is the single canonical source of truth for audio file extensions explicitly specified as `FileExtensions.MusicFileExtensions`? [Completeness, Spec §FR-001]
- [ ] CHK003 - Are handling requirements defined for both zero-byte (empty) files and corrupt/unreadable audio headers? [Completeness, Spec §FR-005]
- [ ] CHK004 - Are player demuxer and format hint mapping requirements specified for all registered extensions? [Completeness, Spec §FR-004]
- [ ] CHK005 - Are technical metadata fields (duration, bitrate, sample rate, channels) explicitly required to be extracted across all formats? [Completeness, Spec §FR-003]

---

## 2. Requirement Clarity & Ambiguity

- [ ] CHK006 - Is the distinction between permanent extraction failures (corrupt/unsupported/empty) and transient errors (timeout/I/O) unambiguously defined? [Clarity, Contract CTR-FMT-ERR-001]
- [ ] CHK007 - Is the database exclusion policy for corrupt/unsupported files clearly stated without ambiguity? [Clarity, Spec §FR-005, Plan §Slice 2]
- [ ] CHK008 - Are LibVLC playback demuxer hints versus native demuxers unambiguously distinguished for container formats? [Clarity, Contract CTR-FMT-002]
- [ ] CHK009 - Is "zero duplicate extension lists" quantified with an explicit prohibition rule? [Clarity, Spec §FR-001]

---

## 3. Requirement Consistency & Architectural Alignment

- [ ] CHK010 - Do the requirements align with the "Existing Code Is Truth" principle by evolving `FileExtensions`, `AtlMetadataService`, and `LibVlcAudioPlayerService` without parallel services? [Consistency, Plan §Constitution Check]
- [ ] CHK011 - Does the data model preserve the existing SQLite `Song` schema without requiring conflicting migrations or new database tables? [Consistency, Data Model §1]
- [ ] CHK012 - Are the 3 vertical implementation slices strictly aligned end-to-end without isolated horizontal tasks? [Consistency, Plan §Vertical Slices]
- [ ] CHK013 - Do the format capabilities match between Scanner, Metadata Service and Audio Player Service contracts? [Consistency, Contract CTR-FMT-001, CTR-FMT-002]

---

## 4. Acceptance Criteria & Measurability

- [ ] CHK014 - Can 100% format parity across Scanner, Metadata Service and Player be objectively verified via automated unit/integration tests? [Measurability, Spec §SC-001]
- [ ] CHK015 - Is the zero-duplicate extension rule testable through automated reflection or architectural test assertions? [Measurability, Spec §SC-002]
- [ ] CHK016 - Can the error isolation outcome (zero unhandled exceptions on corrupt/empty files) be objectively measured? [Measurability, Spec §SC-003]
- [ ] CHK017 - Is the performance criterion (< 50ms average extraction time per local track) verifiable through benchmark or execution metrics? [Measurability, Spec §SC-004]

---

## 5. Scenario & Edge Case Coverage

- [ ] CHK018 - Are DSD formats (`.dsf` and `.dff`) explicitly covered with their respective tagging and playback requirements? [Edge Case, Spec §Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK019 - Is the handling of Musepack dual demuxers (SV7 vs SV8) specified via content probing? [Edge Case, Contract CTR-FMT-002]
- [ ] CHK020 - Are empty file (0 bytes) scenarios covered with explicit classification codes? [Edge Case, Contract CTR-FMT-ERR-001]
- [ ] CHK021 - Is the scenario of mismatched/renamed extensions (e.g. MP3 renamed to .wav) addressed with magic byte inspection requirements? [Edge Case, Spec §Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK022 - Is the player behavior upon encountering a corrupt file during live playback specified without crashing the queue? [Edge Case, Contract CTR-FMT-ERR-002]

---

## 6. Non-Functional & Operational Readiness

- [ ] CHK023 - Are memory and CPU resource constraints defined to prevent buffer underruns during Hi-Res/DSD playback? [Non-Functional, Plan §Technical Context]
- [ ] CHK024 - Is offline playback and inspection capability guaranteed without external network dependencies? [Non-Functional, Plan §Constitution Check]
- [ ] CHK025 - Are Whole-Solution Validation commands (`dotnet build Resonance.sln`, `dotnet test`) established as mandatory merge gates? [Quality Gate, Plan §Constitution Check]

---

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after reviewer inspection confirms that the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied.
- Leave items unchecked (`[ ]`) during requirements authoring and planning; items are evaluated during review.
- `/speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a quality gate and must not modify markers.
- Items are numbered sequentially (CHK001 to CHK025) for direct reference during Pull Request reviews.
